claim: The C. elegans nervous system comprises a sparse neural network with over 6000 different chemically and electrically coupled cell pairs.
source: As one example, even in this small (<400 neurons) nervous system, which comprises a sparse neural network, the number of different chemically and electrically coupled cell pairs is large, over 6000.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion in the introduction, drawing on established knowledge of C. elegans connectome.

claim: Each C. elegans neuron connects to multiple (10 or more) other cells including neurons, muscles, and other end organs.
source: In C. elegans, each neuron connects to multiple (10 or more) other cells — neurons, muscles, and other end organs.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on established knowledge of C. elegans nervous system connectivity.

claim: 69% of chemical synapses in C. elegans hermaphrodites are polyadic.
source: These might be accounted for if coincident signals from several appropriate postsynaptic target cells increase the probability of presynapse formation. Prior studies in C. elegans have implicated interactions with local, albeit non-neuronal, cells in increasing the probability of synapse formation (Colón-Ramos et al., 2007; Shen and Bargmann, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the prevalence of polyadic synapses, supported by citation to prior work.

claim: 66% of chemical synapses in C. elegans males are polyadic.
source: Another feature of the C. elegans nervous system, the prevalence of polyadic chemical synapses (69% in hermaphrodites and 66% in males).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the prevalence of polyadic synapses in males.

claim: The C. elegans genome contains 106 genes encoding transmembrane or secreted proteins with extracellular protein interaction domains.
source: The C. elegans genome contains 106 genes encoding transmembrane or secreted proteins with extracellular protein interaction domains — a structure expected for neural cell-surface recognition molecules (Hobert, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Hobert, 2013.

claim: Many C. elegans presumptive cell adhesion genes are conserved in higher animals and their counterparts have been shown to be involved in synapse formation or stabilization.
source: Many of these presumptive cell adhesion genes are conserved in higher animals and their counterparts have been shown to be involved in synapse formation or stabilization (de Wit and Ghosh, 2016).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to de Wit and Ghosh, 2016.

claim: HOA is a male-specific sensory neuron.
source: For in-depth analysis of circuit formation, we focused on a male-specific circuit that consists of a male-specific sensory neuron, HOA, a sex-shared sensory/interneuron, PHC (a left/right pair of neurons, PHCL and PHCR), and a sex-shared interneuron, AVG (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion in the results section.

claim: PHC is a sex-shared sensory/interneuron that exists as a left/right pair (PHCL and PHCR).
source: For in-depth analysis of circuit formation, we focused on a male-specific circuit that consists of a male-specific sensory neuron, HOA, a sex-shared sensory/interneuron, PHC (a left/right pair of neurons, PHCL and PHCR), and a sex-shared interneuron, AVG (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion in the results section.

claim: AVG is a sex-shared interneuron.
source: For in-depth analysis of circuit formation, we focused on a male-specific circuit that consists of a male-specific sensory neuron, HOA, a sex-shared sensory/interneuron, PHC (a left/right pair of neurons, PHCL and PHCR), and a sex-shared interneuron, AVG (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion in the results section.

claim: The axons of HOA, PHC, and AVG are highly associated with each other to make a bundle within the male pre-anal ganglion.
source: This circuit has two properties: (1) the axons of the three neurons are highly associated with each other to make a bundle within the male pre-anal ganglion (Figure 1B and C);
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion and supported by reference to electron micrograph data shown in Figure 1B and C.

claim: The HOA axon forms en passant dyadic chemical synapses onto AVG and PHC in the pre-anal ganglion region.
source: (2) in this region, the HOA axon forms en passant dyadic chemical synapses onto AVG and PHC (Figure 1B and D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion and supported by reference to electron micrograph data shown in Figure 1B and D.

claim: In one animal reconstructed by electron microscopy, there are approximately 11 clusters of HOA presynaptic densities comprised of 44 synapses with AVG and 46 synapses with PHC.
source: (In one animal reconstructed by electron microscopy, there are ~11 clusters of HOA presynaptic densities comprised of 44 synapses with AVG and 46 synapses with PHC (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy reconstruction data provided in Supplementary file 1.

claim: The PHC axon forms dyadic synapses onto AVG and HOA.
source: The PHC axon also forms dyadic synapses onto AVG and HOA.)
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy data.

claim: HOA has many other synaptic targets outside the pre-anal ganglion region including male-specific neurons PVZ, PCA, and some ray sensory neurons.
source: Outside of this region, HOA has many other synaptic targets including male-specific neurons, PVZ, PCA, and some ray sensory neurons (WormWiring: http://wormwiring.org).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by reference to WormWiring database.

claim: AVG expresses three neural cell adhesion genes: casy-1, rig-6, and sax-3.
source: AVG, which is mostly postsynaptic to the other neurons, expressed three neural cell adhesion genes in our expression dataset, casy-1, rig-6, and sax-3 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on expression analysis shown in Figure 1E.

claim: casy-1(tm718) is a null mutant allele.
source: We used null mutant alleles, casy-1(tm718), rig-6(gk438569) and sax-3(ky123).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the nature of the mutant allele used.

claim: rig-6(gk438569) is a null mutant allele.
source: We used null mutant alleles, casy-1(tm718), rig-6(gk438569) and sax-3(ky123).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the nature of the mutant allele used.

claim: sax-3(ky123) is a null mutant allele.
source: We used null mutant alleles, casy-1(tm718), rig-6(gk438569) and sax-3(ky123).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the nature of the mutant allele used.

claim: rig-6(ok1589) is a hypomorphic allele predicted to affect three out of four isoforms of RIG-6.
source: For rig-6, we also used a hypomorphic rig-6(ok1589) allele, which is predicted to affect three out of four isoforms of RIG-6.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the nature of the mutant allele used.

claim: In wild type, multiple RAB-3 puncta are evenly spaced throughout the HOA process.
source: In wild type, multiple RAB-3 puncta were evenly spaced throughout the HOA process (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Mutations in casy-1 and rig-6 disrupt normal RAB-3 puncta distribution, often exhibiting gaps containing fewer or smaller puncta.
source: All mutations disrupted normal puncta distribution: mutants for casy-1 and rig-6 often exhibited gaps containing fewer or smaller puncta, whereas in mutants lacking sax-3, the number of RAB-3 puncta was increased due to extra branching of the HOA axon (Figure 1F and G, and Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1F, G and supplements.

claim: In sax-3 mutants, the number of RAB-3 puncta is increased due to extra branching of the HOA axon.
source: All mutations disrupted normal puncta distribution: mutants for casy-1 and rig-6 often exhibited gaps containing fewer or smaller puncta, whereas in mutants lacking sax-3, the number of RAB-3 puncta was increased due to extra branching of the HOA axon (Figure 1F and G, and Figure 1—figure supplements 2 and 3).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1F, G and supplements.

claim: SAX-3/Robo is a transmembrane protein with immunoglobulin (Ig) domains.
source: SAX-3/Robo is a transmembrane protein with immunoglobulin (Ig) domains and is known to function in axon guidance of multiple types of neurons (Zallen et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Zallen et al., 1999.

claim: SAX-3/Robo functions in axon guidance of multiple types of neurons.
source: SAX-3/Robo is a transmembrane protein with immunoglobulin (Ig) domains and is known to function in axon guidance of multiple types of neurons (Zallen et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Zallen et al., 1999.

claim: The extra branching phenotype in sax-3 mutants is likely one of the axon guidance defects.
source: Thus it is likely that the extra branching phenotype we observed is one of the axon guidance defects in sax-3 mutants, which we do not pursue further here.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on known functions of SAX-3 and observed phenotypes.

claim: RIG-6/contactin is a GPI-anchored protein belonging to the Ig superfamily.
source: GPI-anchored RIG-6/contactin belongs to the Ig superfamily and its loss leads to axon guidance defects of sensory and motorneurons in C. elegans (Katidou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Katidou et al., 2013.

claim: Loss of RIG-6 leads to axon guidance defects of sensory and motorneurons in C. elegans.
source: GPI-anchored RIG-6/contactin belongs to the Ig superfamily and its loss leads to axon guidance defects of sensory and motorneurons in C. elegans (Katidou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Katidou et al., 2013.

claim: CASY-1/calsyntenin is a cadherin domain-containing transmembrane protein.
source: CASY-1/calsyntenin is a cadherin domain-containing transmembrane protein.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the protein structure.

claim: Mammalian calsyntenin-3 induces in vitro presynapse differentiation when overexpressed postsynaptically.
source: One of its mammalian homologs, calsyntenin-3, has been shown to induce in vitro presynapse differentiation when overexpressed postsynaptically (Pettem et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Pettem et al., 2013.

claim: In casy-1 and rig-6 mutants, the HOA and AVG axons are frequently detached from each other.
source: Indeed, in casy-1 and rig-6 mutants, the HOA and AVG axons were frequently detached from each other (Figure 1H and I).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1H and I.

claim: The axonal segments of HOA detached from AVG have smaller and fewer presynaptic puncta than those contacting AVG.
source: Moreover, the axonal segments of HOA detached from AVG had smaller and fewer presynaptic puncta than those contacting AVG (Figure 1H,J and K).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1H, J and K.

claim: In wild type animals, detached axon segments contain smaller and fewer puncta, even though this occurs rarely.
source: This phenotypic association of axon fasciculation and presynaptic pattern was not due to mutational effects, because in wild type animals we also observed, even though rarely, that detached axon segments contained smaller and fewer puncta (Figure 1J and K).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on quantitative analysis of fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 1J and K.

claim: The HOA presynapse puncta pattern is tightly associated with contacts between HOA and AVG axons.
source: Therefore, the HOA presynapse puncta pattern is tightly associated with contacts between HOA and AVG axons, and the gap phenotype we observed in mCherry::RAB-3 labeled presynaptic structures originates most likely from frequent HOA-AVG defasciculation in mutant animals.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observed correlation between axon contact and puncta pattern in both wild type and mutants.

claim: The gap phenotype in mCherry::RAB-3 labeled presynaptic structures originates most likely from frequent HOA-AVG defasciculation in mutant animals.
source: Therefore, the HOA presynapse puncta pattern is tightly associated with contacts between HOA and AVG axons, and the gap phenotype we observed in mCherry::RAB-3 labeled presynaptic structures originates most likely from frequent HOA-AVG defasciculation in mutant animals.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observed correlation between axon contact and puncta pattern.

claim: In the wild type animal reconstructed by electron microscopy, the PHCL and PHCR axons are separated over 30% of their lengths by only one-neurite distance.
source: This measurement was sensitive enough to detect subtle defasciculation events: in the wild type animal reconstructed by electron microscopy, the PHCL and PHCR axons, for example, are separated over 30% of their lengths by only one-neurite distance, and similar measurement of defasciculation was observed using fluorescence images (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy reconstruction data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: In casy-1 mutants, the HOA axon is frequently detached from the PHC-AVG axon bundle.
source: We found that the axon fasciculation defects of casy-1 and rig-6 mutants were distinguishable from each other: in mutants lacking casy-1, the HOA axon was frequently detached from the PHC-AVG axon bundle (Figure 2B and E),
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2B and E.

claim: In rig-6 mutants (either ok1589 or gk438569), both HOA and PHC axons are detached from AVG, but the fasciculation of HOA and PHC is not affected.
source: whereas in rig-6 mutants (either ok1589 or gk438569), both HOA and PHC axons were detached from AVG, but the fasciculation of HOA and PHC was not affected (Figure 2C and E, and Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2C, E and supplement 2.

claim: The double mutants of casy-1 and rig-6 show an additive phenotype, in which all three axons are disassociated.
source: The double mutants of casy-1 and rig-6 showed an additive phenotype, in which all three axons were disassociated (Figure 2D and E).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 2D and E.

claim: casy-1 and rig-6 are required for proper wiring of the HOA-AVG-PHC circuit, but may function differently to achieve this goal.
source: Taken together, the results indicate that casy-1 and rig-6 are required for proper wiring of the HOA-AVG-PHC circuit, but may function differently to achieve this goal.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the distinct phenotypes observed in casy-1 and rig-6 mutants.

claim: AVG grows its axon in the embryo and pioneers the right tract of the ventral nerve cord.
source: AVG grows its axon in the embryo and pioneers the right tract of the ventral nerve cord (Durbin, 1987).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Durbin, 1987.

claim: During the fourth larval stage (L4), in males but not hermaphrodites, PHC extends a process that follows along the axon of AVG.
source: During the fourth larval stage (L4), in males but not hermaphrodites, PHC extends a process that follows along the axon of AVG (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on developmental imaging data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: During the L4-adult transition, HOA extends its axon along the PHC-AVG bundle.
source: Later, during the L4-adult transition, HOA extends its axon along the PHC-AVG bundle (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on developmental imaging data shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: Axonal contact between HOA and AVG is promoted by PHC.
source: Thus, it is possible that axonal contact between HOA and AVG is promoted by PHC.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the developmental timing of axon extension.

claim: When PHC is ablated, axonal contact between HOA and AVG is compromised, showing a fasciculation defect similar to that observed in casy-1 and rig-6 mutants.
source: When PHC was ablated, axonal contact between HOA and AVG was compromised, showing a fasciculation defect similar to that observed in casy-1 and rig-6 mutants (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell ablation experiments shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: PHC-AVG axonal contact is not affected by HOA ablation.
source: However, PHC-AVG or HOA-PHC axonal contact was not affected by HOA or AVG ablation, respectively (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell ablation experiments shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: HOA-PHC axonal contact is not affected by AVG ablation.
source: However, PHC-AVG or HOA-PHC axonal contact was not affected by HOA or AVG ablation, respectively (Figure 2H and I).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell ablation experiments shown in Figure 2H and I.

claim: There is an affinity between HOA and PHC.
source: These results suggest there is an affinity between HOA and PHC and raise the possibility that in rig-6 mutants, the primary defect is loss of adhesion between PHC and AVG, while HOA separates from AVG because of adhesion to PHC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the cell ablation experiments.

claim: In rig-6 mutants, the primary defect is loss of adhesion between PHC and AVG, while HOA separates from AVG because of adhesion to PHC.
source: These results suggest there is an affinity between HOA and PHC and raise the possibility that in rig-6 mutants, the primary defect is loss of adhesion between PHC and AVG, while HOA separates from AVG because of adhesion to PHC.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis based on the cell ablation experiments and mutant phenotypes.

claim: Full-length casy-1 cDNA expressed in postsynaptic AVG, but not presynaptic HOA or PHC, rescues axon fasciculation defects in casy-1 mutants.
source: Cell-specific rescue experiments showed that full-length casy-1 cDNA when expressed in postsynaptic AVG, but not presynaptic HOA or PHC, rescued axon fasciculation defects in casy-1 mutants (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 3A.

claim: rig-6 cDNA only when expressed in AVG rescues fasciculation defects of rig-6 mutants.
source: Similarly, rig-6 cDNA only when expressed in AVG rescued fasciculation defects of rig-6 mutants (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 3B.

claim: YFP::RIG-6 is localized to the AVG axon, but in the cell body is mainly cytoplasmic.
source: YFP::RIG-6 was also localized to the axon, but in the cell body was mainly cytoplasmic (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging of tagged protein shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Both CASY-1 and RIG-6 function in postsynaptic AVG, possibly by transmembrane adhesion activity of axonally localized proteins, to make an axon fascicle with the presynaptic neurons.
source: Taken together, both CASY-1 and RIG-6 function in postsynaptic AVG, possibly by transmembrane adhesion activity of axonally localized proteins, to make an axon fascicle with the presynaptic neurons.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the cell-specific rescue experiments and protein localization data.

claim: CASY-1 contains two cadherin domains and a Laminin, Neurexin, Sex hormone-binding globulin (LNS) domain in its extracellular region.
source: CASY-1 contains two cadherin domains and a Laminin, Neurexin, Sex hormone-binding globulin (LNS) domain in its extracellular region (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the protein structure shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The full-length CASY-1 transgene rescues the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
source: The full-length (Full) or two cadherin domains-deleted (ΔCads) transgene rescued the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments.

claim: The two cadherin domains-deleted (ΔCads) CASY-1 transgene rescues the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
source: The full-length (Full) or two cadherin domains-deleted (ΔCads) transgene rescued the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments.

claim: The LNS domain-deleted (ΔLNS) CASY-1 transgene fails to rescue the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
source: However, the LNS domain-deleted (ΔLNS) or all extracellular domains-deleted (ΔNt) transgene failed to rescue the defect (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The all extracellular domains-deleted (ΔNt) CASY-1 transgene fails to rescue the fasciculation defect of casy-1 mutants.
source: However, the LNS domain-deleted (ΔLNS) or all extracellular domains-deleted (ΔNt) transgene failed to rescue the defect (Figure 4A and B).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments shown in Figure 4A and B.

claim: The LNS domain of CASY-1 is essential for axon fasciculation, but the cadherin domains are dispensable for this function.
source: Thus, the LNS domain of CASY-1 is essential for axon fasciculation, but the cadherin domains are dispensable for this function.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the domain deletion rescue experiments.

claim: RIG-6 has six Ig domains and four fibronectin type III (FN[III]) domains in its extracellular region.
source: RIG-6 has six Ig domains and four fibronectin type III (FN[III]) domains in its extracellular region (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion about the protein structure shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The full-length RIG-6 transgene rescues the fasciculation defect of rig-6 mutants.
source: The full-length (Full) or four FN[III] domains-deleted (ΔFN[III]) transgene rescued the fasciculation defect of rig-6 mutants,
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments.

claim: The four FN[III] domains-deleted (ΔFN[III]) RIG-6 transgene rescues the fasciculation defect of rig-6 mutants.
source: The full-length (Full) or four FN[III] domains-deleted (ΔFN[III]) transgene rescued the fasciculation defect of rig-6 mutants,
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments.

claim: Ig domains-deleted (Δ1-3Ig and Δ4-6Ig) RIG-6 transgenes cannot rescue the fasciculation defect of rig-6 mutants.
source: whereas Ig domains-deleted (Δ1-3Ig and Δ4-6Ig) transgenes could not (Figure 4C and D),
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments shown in Figure 4C and D.

claim: The Ig domains of RIG-6 are required for axon fasciculation.
source: indicating that the Ig domains of RIG-6 are required for axon fasciculation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the domain deletion rescue experiments.

claim: The LNS domain of CASY-1 and the Ig domains of RIG-6 are functionally responsible for axon fasciculation, possibly by acting as the binding sites for trans-interacting partners.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the LNS domain of CASY-1 and the Ig domains of RIG-6 are functionally responsible for axon fasciculation, possibly by acting as the binding sites for trans-interacting partners.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the domain deletion rescue experiments.

claim: bam-2(cy6) mutants show a gap phenotype similar to the casy-1 mutant defect.
source: Among null mutants for the five genes expressed in HOA in our expression dataset (Figure 1E), bam-2(cy6) mutants were identified as showing a gap phenotype similar to the casy-1 mutant defect (Figure 5A and B, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 5A, B and supplement 1.

claim: BAM-2 is a neurexin-related transmembrane protein that regulates axonal branch extension of hermaphrodite-specific VC ventral cord motorneurons in C. elegans.
source: BAM-2 is a neurexin-related transmembrane protein that regulates axonal branch extension of hermaphrodite-specific VC ventral cord motorneurons in C. elegans (Colavita and Tessier-Lavigne, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Colavita and Tessier-Lavigne, 2003.

claim: Calsyntenin-3 was shown to be an α-neurexin interacting partner.
source: In a previous study, a CASY-1 homolog, calsyntenin-3, was shown to be an α-neurexin interacting partner, raising the possibility that BAM-2 is a presynaptic binding partner of CASY-1 (Pettem et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Pettem et al., 2013.

claim: Animals lacking bam-2 show axon fasciculation defects similar to the phenotype of casy-1 mutants.
source: Animals lacking bam-2 showed axon fasciculation defects similar to the phenotype of casy-1 mutants (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Double mutation of casy-1 and bam-2 does not enhance the axon fasciculation defect, suggesting that these genes act in the same genetic pathway.
source: Double mutation of casy-1 and bam-2 did not enhance the axon fasciculation defect, suggesting that these genes act in the same genetic pathway (Figure 5C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion and conclusion based on double mutant analysis shown in Figure 5C and D.

claim: Full-length bam-2 cDNA expressed in HOA, but not PHC, rescues axon fasciculation defects in bam-2 mutants.
source: Cell-specific rescue showed that full-length bam-2 cDNA expressed in HOA, but not PHC, rescued axon fasciculation defects in bam-2 mutants (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Flag-tagged CASY-1 binds to V5-tagged BAM-2.
source: Finally, we tested protein interaction of CASY-1 and BAM-2 in a co-immunoprecipitation assay and found that Flag-tagged CASY-1 binds to V5-tagged BAM-2 (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on co-immunoprecipitation assay shown in Figure 5F.

claim: NRX-1, a canonical neurexin protein in C. elegans, does not bind to CASY-1.
source: In contrast, NRX-1, a canonical neurexin protein in C. elegans, did not bind to CASY-1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on co-immunoprecipitation assay shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.

claim: BAM-2 is a functional presynaptic binding partner of CASY-1 for axon fasciculation.
source: These results suggest that BAM-2 is a functional presynaptic binding partner of CASY-1 for axon fasciculation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the genetic, rescue, and biochemical interaction data.

claim: sax-7(nj48) mutants show the gap phenotype in HOA presynaptic puncta.
source: Accordingly, we examined HOA presynaptic puncta in null mutants for the five cell adhesion genes expressed in PHC and found sax-7(nj48) showed the gap phenotype (Figure 6A and B, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 6A, B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: SAX-7/L1CAM is a transmembrane protein with six Ig and five FN[III] domains in its extracellular region.
source: SAX-7/L1CAM, a transmembrane protein with six Ig and five FN[III] domains in its extracellular region, is required in C. elegans for maintenance of neuronal position including the cell body and axon (Zallen et al., 1999; Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Zallen et al., 1999; Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008.

claim: SAX-7/L1CAM is required in C. elegans for maintenance of neuronal position including the cell body and axon.
source: SAX-7/L1CAM, a transmembrane protein with six Ig and five FN[III] domains in its extracellular region, is required in C. elegans for maintenance of neuronal position including the cell body and axon (Zallen et al., 1999; Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Zallen et al., 1999; Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008.

claim: SAX-7 has two isoforms – a long form with six Ig domains (SAX-7L) and a short form with four Ig domains (SAX-7S).
source: It has two isoforms – a long form with six Ig domains (SAX-7L) and a short form with four Ig domains (SAX-7S), where SAX-7S is shown to have more adhesive activity for cellular contact (Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008.

claim: SAX-7S is shown to have more adhesive activity for cellular contact than SAX-7L.
source: It has two isoforms – a long form with six Ig domains (SAX-7L) and a short form with four Ig domains (SAX-7S), where SAX-7S is shown to have more adhesive activity for cellular contact (Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Sasakura et al., 2005; Pocock et al., 2008.

claim: Some of the L1 family proteins including L1CAM are known to interact in trans with the RIG-6 ortholog contactin.
source: Some of the L1 family proteins including L1CAM are known to interact in trans with the RIG-6 ortholog contactin (reviewed in Shimoda and Watanabe, 2009).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to a review by Shimoda and Watanabe, 2009.

claim: In sax-7(nj48) mutants, the HOA and PHC axons are detached from AVG, but the HOA-PHC fasciculation is intact, which is similar to the phenotype of rig-6 mutants.
source: First, in sax-7(nj48) mutants, the HOA and PHC axons were detached from AVG, but the HOA-PHC fasciculation was intact, which is similar to the phenotype of rig-6 mutants (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging data shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The double mutant phenotype of rig-6;sax-7 animals is similar to that of rig-6 or sax-7 single mutants, suggesting that they act genetically in the same pathway.
source: Second, the double mutant phenotype of rig-6;sax-7 animals was similar to that of rig-6 or sax-7 single mutants, suggesting that they act genetically in the same pathway (Figure 6C and D).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion and conclusion based on double mutant analysis shown in Figure 6C and D.

claim: The short form SAX-7S expressed in PHC, but not in HOA, rescues axon fasciculation defects in sax-7 mutants.
source: Third, in cell-specific rescue experiments, the short form SAX-7S expressed in PHC, but not in HOA, rescued axon fasciculation defects in sax-7 mutants, whereas SAX-7L failed to rescue both in PHC and HOA (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: SAX-7L fails to rescue axon fasciculation defects in sax-7 mutants both in PHC and HOA.
source: Third, in cell-specific rescue experiments, the short form SAX-7S expressed in PHC, but not in HOA, rescued axon fasciculation defects in sax-7 mutants, whereas SAX-7L failed to rescue both in PHC and HOA (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on cell-specific rescue experiments shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Flag-tagged RIG-6 binds to V5-tagged SAX-7S.
source: Finally, co-immunoprecipitation assay showed that Flag-tagged RIG-6 binds to V5-tagged SAX-7S (Figure 6F).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on co-immunoprecipitation assay shown in Figure 6F.

claim: SAX-7 protein is detected in PHC, but not in HOA or AVG, when examined using a fosmid-based reporter.
source: SAX-7 protein was detected in PHC, but not in HOA or AVG, when we examined a fosmid-based reporter to better define the neurons expressing sax-7 (Figure 6—figure supplement 1).

claim: Ectopic expression of SAX-7S in HOA rescues the fasciculation defects caused by PHC ablation.
source: Indeed, we found that the ectopic expression of SAX-7S in HOA rescued the fasciculation defects caused by PHC ablation (Figure 6G and H).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments in PHC-ablated animals shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: Ectopic expression of SAX-7S in HOA rescues fasciculation defects in a casy-1 mutant, but not in a rig-6 mutant.
source: Moreover, a similar rescuing effect was observed in a casy-1 mutant, but not in a rig-6 mutant (Figure 6G and H), further supporting the conclusion that SAX-7S binds to RIG-6 and this binding mediates axon fasciculation.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on rescue experiments shown in Figure 6G and H.

claim: SAX-7S binds to RIG-6 and this binding mediates axon fasciculation.
source: Moreover, a similar rescuing effect was observed in a casy-1 mutant, but not in a rig-6 mutant (Figure 6G and H), further supporting the conclusion that SAX-7S binds to RIG-6 and this binding mediates axon fasciculation.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the genetic, rescue, and biochemical interaction data.

claim: The male-specific HOA sensory neuron is required for the vulva location step of the mating sequence.
source: The male-specific HOA sensory neuron is required for the vulva location step of this sequence (Liu and Sternberg, 1995).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Liu and Sternberg, 1995.

claim: Genetic or laser ablation of AVG or PHC leads to defects in vulva location.
source: Recently, it has been found that genetic or laser ablation of AVG or PHC also leads to defects in vulva location (Oren-Suissa et al., 2016; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2017a).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Oren-Suissa et al., 2016; Serrano-Saiz et al., 2017a.

claim: Mutant males for casy-1, rig-6, bam-2, and sax-7 all exhibit vulva location defects.
source: We examined mating behavior of mutant males for casy-1, rig-6, bam-2, and sax-7, and all exhibited vulva location defects (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral assays shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Double mutants (casy-1;rig-6, casy-1;bam-2, and rig-6;sax-7) show similar vulva location behavioral defects.
source: Double mutants (casy-1;rig-6, casy-1;bam-2, and rig-6;sax-7) also showed similar behavioral defects.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral assays.

claim: Cell-autonomous expression of the cDNAs in the corresponding mutants partially restores vulva location behavior.
source: Cell-autonomous expression of the cDNAs in the corresponding mutants partially restored vulva location behavior (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral rescue experiments shown in Figure 7A.

claim: The male's ability to respond to hermaphrodite contact is not affected in casy-1, rig-6, and bam-2 mutants, with the exception of the sax-7 mutation.
source: These defects appear to be specific to the vulva location step, since the male's ability to respond to hermaphrodite contact, the first step of the sequence, was not affected, with the exception of the sax-7 mutation (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral assays shown in Figure 7B.

claim: sax-7 is expressed in some of the ray sensory neurons that are known to function in the response step.
source: In our expression analysis, sax-7 was also expressed in some of the ray sensory neurons that are known to function in the response step (data not shown), raising the possibility that sax-7 function in ray neurons is required for the response behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on expression analysis, with speculation about its functional significance.

claim: Expression of SAX-7S in PHC partially rescues defects of sax-7 mutants in the response to contact.
source: Interestingly, expression of SAX-7S in PHC partially rescued defects of sax-7 mutants in the response to contact (Figure 7B), suggesting that response behavior also requires sax-7 function in PHC.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral rescue experiments shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Response behavior requires sax-7 function in PHC.
source: Interestingly, expression of SAX-7S in PHC partially rescued defects of sax-7 mutants in the response to contact (Figure 7B), suggesting that response behavior also requires sax-7 function in PHC.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the behavioral rescue experiments.

claim: The cell adhesion proteins regulate male mating behavior by mediating the formation of a normally responsive sensory circuit.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that the cell adhesion proteins described above regulate male mating behavior by mediating the formation of a normally responsive sensory circuit.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the behavioral and circuit formation data.

claim: Three independent pathways promote connectivity between HOA and AVG.
source: We found that three independent pathways appear to promote this connectivity.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the genetic and ablation experiments.

claim: One pathway involves interactions between cell surface proteins on the processes of HOA and AVG.
source: One involves interactions between cell surface proteins on the processes of HOA and AVG.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the CASY-1/BAM-2 interaction data.

claim: A second pathway involves another sensory neuron PHC and interactions between cell surface proteins on PHC and AVG.
source: A second involves another sensory neuron that is also postsynaptic to HOA, PHC, and interactions between cell surface proteins on PHC and AVG.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the RIG-6/SAX-7S interaction data.

claim: A third, basal pathway results in approximately 50% level of fasciculation and synapse formation between HOA and AVG in the absence of the other two pathways.
source: A third pathway we did not identify by itself gives an approximately 50% level of fasciculation and synapse formation between HOA and AVG (Figure 8).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the residual fasciculation observed in double mutants, shown in Figure 8.

claim: Synapse formation between HOA and AVG takes place during the late period of the last, L4, larval stage, when HOA sends out a process along AVG.
source: Synapse formation between HOA and AVG takes place during the late period of the last, L4, larval stage, when HOA sends out a process along AVG.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on developmental observations.

claim: PHC grows a process fasciculated to AVG before HOA.
source: PHC grows a process fasciculated to AVG before HOA.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on developmental observations.

claim: The role of PHC in promoting HOA fasciculation to AVG is explained by an interaction between HOA and PHC, the molecular basis of which remains to be identified.
source: The role of PHC in promoting HOA fasciculation to AVG is explained by an interaction between HOA and PHC, the molecular basis of which remains to be identified.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion with acknowledgment that the molecular mechanism is unknown.

claim: Epithelial cells of the vulva promote formation of neuromuscular junctions between the HSN motor neuron and vulval muscles.
source: Epithelial cells of the vulva promote formation of neuromuscular junctions between the HSN motor neuron and vulval muscles (Shen and Bargmann, 2003).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Shen and Bargmann, 2003.

claim: The interaction between HSN and vulval epithelium involves binding between Ig-domain cell adhesion molecules SYG-2, expressed by the epithelium, and SYG-1, expressed by HSN.
source: The interaction involves binding between Ig-domain cell adhesion molecules SYG-2, expressed by the epithelium, and SYG-1, expressed by HSN (Özkan et al., 2014; Shen et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Özkan et al., 2014; Shen et al., 2004.

claim: Glial cells promote connection between AIY and RIA interneurons through the UNC-6/netrin pathway.
source: Glial cells promote connection between AIY and RIA interneurons through the UNC-6/netrin pathway (Colón-Ramos et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Colón-Ramos et al., 2007.

claim: The combined involvement of more than two cells may be a significant way that a combinatorial complexity can be introduced into the mechanism of synaptic specificity.
source: The combined involvement of more than two cells may be a significant way that a combinatorial complexity can be introduced into the mechanism of synaptic specificity.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation about the significance of multi-cell involvement in synapse formation.

claim: The pathway that can give rise to 50% of wild type level of fasciculation even in the absence of the identified cell adhesion proteins could be the cell lineage itself.
source: We speculate that the pathway that can give rise to a 50% of wild type level of fasciculation even in the absence of the cell adhesion proteins we identified could be the cell lineage itself, which places cells at reproducible locations with reproducible sets of neighbors.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the nature of the basal pathway.

claim: Unless a cell migrates away from its site of birth, it has a limited number of choices for process neighborhoods.
source: As pointed out previously, unless a cell migrates away from its site of birth, it has a limited number of choices for process neighborhoods (White, 1985; White et al., 1983).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to White, 1985; White et al., 1983.

claim: Involvement of a third cell means lineage specification of that cell also contributes to specifying connectivity.
source: Involvement of a third cell means lineage specification of that cell also contributes to specifying connectivity.
evidence: This is stated as an inference about how cell lineage contributes to connectivity.

claim: Simultaneous removal of two sets of adhesion protein interactions reduces the level of fasciculation and hence synapse formation by only 50%.
source: For connection of HOA to AVG, simultaneous removal of two sets of adhesion protein interactions reduces the level of fasciculation and hence synapse formation by only 50%.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on the double mutant analysis.

claim: Some of the earliest uncoordinated mutations identified in C. elegans, which define the UNC-6/netrin guidance pathway, affect cells that do not run in defined neighborhoods.
source: It is perhaps telling that some of the earliest uncoordinated mutations identified in C. elegans, which define the UNC-6/netrin guidance pathway and do in fact affect connectivity, affect cells that do not run in defined neighborhoods (Brenner, 1973; Hedgecock et al., 1990).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Brenner, 1973; Hedgecock et al., 1990.

claim: In UNC-6/netrin pathway mutants, the nervous system remains intact and generally functional despite the global role in guidance played by the pathway.
source: Apart from these and some additional effects, in spite of the global role in guidance played by the UNC-6/netrin pathway, in UNC-6/netrin pathway mutants the nervous system remains intact and generally functional.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on known phenotypes of UNC-6/netrin pathway mutants.

claim: Mutations in widely-expressed genes for conserved pathways, such as the neurexin/neuroligin interaction and Slit/Robo signaling, have only mild effects on worm behavior.
source: Mutations in other widely-expressed genes for conserved pathways, such as the neurexin/neuroligin interaction and Slit/Robo signaling, have only mild effects on worm behavior.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on known phenotypes of these mutants.

claim: The nervous system is a robust structure that is based on extensive genetic redundancy.
source: The nervous system is clearly a robust structure that is based on extensive genetic redundancy.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observed mild phenotypes of many mutations.

claim: EM reconstruction shows that in one individual, HOA was fasciculated with AVG over 30 microns.
source: EM reconstruction shows that in one individual, HOA was fasciculated with AVG over 30 microns.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy reconstruction data.

claim: In the fasciculated region, 46 presynaptic densities occur in 11 clusters relatively evenly spaced at intervals averaging 1.7 microns.
source: In the fasciculated region 46 presynaptic densities occur in 11 clusters relatively evenly spaced at intervals averaging 1.7 microns (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy reconstruction data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Presynaptic densities occur at swellings in the HOA process that contain a mitochondrion.
source: They occur at swellings in the HOA process that contained a mitochondrion.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on electron microscopy observations.

claim: The swellings containing mitochondria and presynaptic structures could be observed with a cytoplasmic marker.
source: These swellings could be observed with a cytoplasmic marker (Figure 1H).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on fluorescence imaging shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Absence of mCherry::RAB-3 puncta suggests that components of the presynaptic structure necessary to recruit synaptic vesicles are not assembled at discrete membrane locations.
source: Absence of mCherry::RAB-3 puncta suggests that components of the presynaptic structure necessary to recruit synaptic vesicles are not assembled at discrete membrane locations.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the absence of RAB-3 puncta.

claim: The formation of mCherry::RAB-3 puncta within HOA correlates with apparent fasciculation with AVG and requires AVG contact.
source: The formation of mCherry::RAB-3 puncta within HOA correlated with apparent fasciculation with AVG and required AVG contact, since in wild type they were absent or reduced in rare regions of process separation.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on the correlation observed in wild type animals.

claim: For recruitment of presynaptic components, the contact signal does not require the cell adhesion genes involved in promoting fasciculation.
source: For recruitment of presynaptic components, the contact signal did not require the cell adhesion genes involved in promoting fasciculation, since in the mutants for these genes, puncta appeared normal in regions of contact (Figure 1).
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observation that puncta are normal in contacted regions of mutants, shown in Figure 1.

claim: oig-1 and oig-8 may be necessary for the formation of puncta, because the mutants lacking them exhibit diffused puncta pattern.
source: Of the 13 genes we examined, oig-1 and oig-8 may be necessary for the formation of puncta, because the mutants lacking them exhibited diffused puncta pattern (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the diffused puncta phenotype shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The diffused puncta phenotype in oig-1 and oig-8 mutants is similar to that of animals lacking SYD-2/Liprin-α, which functions in formation of the presynaptic active zone.
source: This diffused puncta phenotype is similar to that of animals lacking SYD-2/Liprin-α, which functions in formation of the presynaptic active zone (Zhen and Jin, 1999), suggesting that oig-1 and oig-8 may be involved in organizing presynaptic structures.
evidence: This is stated as a comparison and inference supported by citation to Zhen and Jin, 1999.

claim: oig-1 and oig-8 may be involved in organizing presynaptic structures.
source: This diffused puncta phenotype is similar to that of animals lacking SYD-2/Liprin-α, which functions in formation of the presynaptic active zone (Zhen and Jin, 1999), suggesting that oig-1 and oig-8 may be involved in organizing presynaptic structures.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the similarity to SYD-2/Liprin-α mutant phenotype.

claim: The cell adhesion genes required for promoting fasciculation between HOA and AVG are homologs of genes that have been shown to be involved in axon outgrowth and synapse formation in mammals.
source: We found that the cell adhesion genes required for promoting fasciculation between HOA and AVG are homologs of genes that have been shown to be involved in axon outgrowth and synapse formation in mammals.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the conservation of these genes.

claim: The molecular architecture of the nervous system is conserved across animals.
source: Just as so much else of the molecular architecture of the nervous system is conserved across animals, so too, it appears, are the molecular tools that establish synaptic connectivity (Bargmann, 1998).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Bargmann, 1998.

claim: The molecular tools that establish synaptic connectivity are conserved across animals.
source: Just as so much else of the molecular architecture of the nervous system is conserved across animals, so too, it appears, are the molecular tools that establish synaptic connectivity (Bargmann, 1998).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Bargmann, 1998.

claim: Connectivity differs profoundly from species to species and accounts for each species' repertoire of behaviors.
source: Yet unlike many other aspects of neural function, such as the mechanisms underlying cellular electrical properties or synaptic transmission, connectivity differs profoundly from species to species and accounts for each species' repertoire of behaviors.
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on general knowledge of nervous system diversity.

claim: The resolution of the paradox of conserved molecular tools but diverse connectivity is the employment of these generic cell-recognition and adhesion tools with different combinations in different places.
source: The resolution of this apparent paradox, of course, is the employment of these generic cell-recognition and adhesion tools with different combinations in different places.
evidence: This is stated as an explanation for how conserved molecules can produce diverse connectivity.

claim: The process of specifying diverse connectivity is analogous to the specification of diverse cell types by a conserved set of transcription factors.
source: The process is analogous to the specification of diverse cell types by a conserved set of transcription factors.
evidence: This is stated as an analogy to explain the mechanism of connectivity specification.

claim: CASY-1/calsyntenin binds to BAM-2/neurexin-related in trans to promote axon-axon adhesion.
source: Our results show that CASY-1/calsyntenin binds to BAM-2/neurexin-related in trans to promote axon-axon adhesion.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the genetic, rescue, and biochemical interaction data.

claim: A similar protein interaction between calsyntenin-3 and α-neurexin has been shown to regulate synapse formation in mammals.
source: A similar protein interaction between calsyntenin-3 and α-neurexin has been shown to regulate synapse formation in mammals (Pettem et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Pettem et al., 2013.

claim: The LNS domain of calsyntenin-3 alone is sufficient to bind α-neurexin.
source: A biochemical study has shown that the LNS domain of calsyntenin-3 alone is sufficient to bind α-neurexin (Lu et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Lu et al., 2014.

claim: In C. elegans, BAM-2 may exist as a related but diverged form of neurexin to act as a functional binding partner of CASY-1/calsyntenin.
source: This suggests that in C. elegans BAM-2 may exist as a related but diverged form of neurexin to act as a functional binding partner of CASY-1/calsyntenin.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the observed binding specificity.

claim: The conserved function of CASY-1/calsyntenin-BAM-2/neurexin-related interaction in neural adhesion and synapse formation is maintained throughout evolution.
source: The conserved function of CASY-1/calsyntenin-BAM-2/neurexin-related interaction in neural adhesion and synapse formation seems to be maintained throughout evolution.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the functional conservation observed.

claim: Protein binding between RIG-6/contactin and SAX-7/L1CAM appears to be molecularly and functionally conserved.
source: Like CASY-1-BAM-2 interaction, protein binding between RIG-6/contactin and SAX-7/L1CAM appears to be molecularly and functionally conserved.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion based on the observed interaction and known conservation.

claim: A number of protein interactions between contactins (six members: contactin-1–6) and L1 family proteins (four members: L1, CHL1, neurofascin and NrCAM) have been found in vertebrates.
source: A number of protein interactions between contactins (six members: contactin-1–6) and L1 family proteins (four members: L1, CHL1, neurofascin and NrCAM) have been found in vertebrates (Shimoda and Watanabe, 2009; Gennarini et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Shimoda and Watanabe, 2009; Gennarini et al., 2017.

claim: Trans-interactions between contactins and L1 family proteins are thought to mediate axon outgrowth via contactin-2 binding to L1 or NrCAM.
source: Trans-interactions between these proteins are thought to mediate axon outgrowth via contactin-2 binding to L1 or NrCAM (Kuhn et al., 1991; Stoeckli et al., 1997)
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Kuhn et al., 1991; Stoeckli et al., 1997.

claim: Trans-interactions between contactins and L1 family proteins are thought to mediate synapse formation via a putative interaction between contactin-5 and NrCAM.
source: and synapse formation via a putative interaction between contactin-5 and NrCAM (Ashrafi et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Ashrafi et al., 2014.

claim: RIG-6-SAX-7 interaction might be mediated via the Ig domains.
source: Our domain analysis of RIG-6 indicates that the extracellular Ig domains, but not the FN[III] domains, are required for axon fasciculation, suggesting that RIG-6-SAX-7 interaction might be mediated via the Ig domains (Figure 4).
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the domain deletion experiments.

claim: Recent studies have revealed the importance of interactions between Ig domains in cell-cell recognition.
source: Recent studies have revealed the importance of interactions between Ig domains in cell-cell recognition (Özkan et al., 2013, 2014; Carrillo et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citations to Özkan et al., 2013, 2014; Carrillo et al., 2015.

claim: It is possible that the Ig domains of RIG-6 interact directly with the Ig domains of SAX-7 to achieve adhesive function.
source: Thus, it is possible that the Ig domains of RIG-6 interact directly with the Ig domains of SAX-7 to achieve adhesive function.
evidence: This is stated as a speculation based on the domain requirements and known importance of Ig domain interactions.

evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Osterhout et al., 2015.

source: some contactins (contactin-4–6) are genetically implicated in autism and other mental disorders (Oguro-Ando et al., 2017).

claim: Neurexin is a well-known neural adhesion protein involved in autism and other cognitive diseases.
source: (3) BAM-2/neurexin-related: neurexin is a well-known neural adhesion protein involved in autism and other cognitive diseases (Südhof, 2008).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Südhof, 2008.

claim: L1 mutations are associated with diverse neurological defects and mental retardation.
source: (4) SAX-7/L1CAM: L1 mutations are associated with diverse neurological defects and mental retardation (Fransen et al., 1997).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion supported by citation to Fransen et al., 1997.

source: In our behavioral assays, loss of these adhesion factors disrupted vulva location behavior during male mating (Figure 7).
evidence: This is stated as a factual assertion based on behavioral assays shown in Figure 7.

claim: The cell adhesion proteins may contribute to behavioral performance, in part, through their adhesive functions in circuit assembly.
source: We propose that the cell adhesion proteins may contribute to behavioral performance, in part, through their adhesive functions in circuit assembly.
